sections.h2: What should an owner know about property tax in Bell County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Bell County is a small, low value housing market in the southeast corner of Kentucky, and its property tax bills are handled by the same set of local offices as in every other Kentucky county: the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets value, the sheriff bills and collects, and the county clerk takes appeals and unpaid bills.

The county sits on the Tennessee and Virginia borders at the Cumberland Gap. Pineville is the seat, Middlesboro is the largest city, and Arjay is a census designated place. Bell County is the only county in Kentucky with both a state resort park, Pine Mountain, and a national park unit, Cumberland Gap National Historical Park. Those protected lands, plus steep ground, shape where houses are built and how far a buyer will drive to one.

sections.h2: How has Bell County's population changed, and why does it affect a sale?
sections.html:
Bell County lost about 5.3 percent of its people between the April 2020 census count of 24,097 and the July 2025 estimate of 22,829. Wikipedia's historical table shows a peak of 47,602 in 1950, so the county today holds roughly half the residents it had seventy years ago.

That history is built into the housing stock. The Census Bureau reports a median owner occupied home value of $89,000 for 2020 to 2024, and a median household income of $31,354, with 31.8 percent of residents in poverty. Median gross rent is $592. Only 41 building permits were issued in 2025.

With values this low, an unpaid tax bill, clerk fees and interest can take a much larger share of a sale price than in a higher value county, so checking the tax status early pays off.

sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Bell County?
sections.html:
Three offices cover most questions, and a fourth takes over after a bill goes delinquent. The list shows what each does under Kentucky's property tax process.

  • The Bell County PVA assesses real estate and takes homestead applications and appeal conferences.
  • The Bell County Sheriff mails bills and collects them, with bills mailed in the fall.
  • The Bell County Clerk, whose office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., records deeds, mortgages and liens, and receives delinquent bills.
  • The county attorney sends the notices that follow a transfer and can arrange installment plans.

The Pineville city government also posts its own property tax page. Since tax year 2020 the Bell County Sheriff's Office has collected City of Pineville property tax on the same bill as the county tax, and the city page lists a real property rate of 27.6 cents per $100 of assessed value. Confirm the current rate with the city before relying on that figure.

The county clerk's recording room matters to sellers for another reason: the Bell County courthouse burned in 1914 and 1918 and was damaged by flooding in 1977, which destroyed stored documents. If an old deed or probate record looks incomplete, ask the clerk what the recorded chain shows.

sections.h2: When are Bell County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills follow the statewide collection cycle in KRS 134.015 unless the Department of Revenue approves a delayed calendar. The sheriff may start collecting after November 1 in some years, and the state then gives 30 days for each stage instead of the normal dates.

On the normal schedule, payment with a 2 percent discount runs through November 1, face value is due from November 2 through December 31, a 5 percent penalty applies in January, and a total of 21 percent applies from February 1 to April 15 when the sheriff's add-on is counted. The Department of Revenue notes that bills are mailed by the sheriff in the fall and collected in the sheriff's office.

Taxes are owed by whoever held the property on January 1, so a Bell County seller who closes in the spring still owes the tax for that year unless the contract assigns it to the buyer. Ask the sheriff for a duplicate if you have not received a bill, since the bill goes to the owner of record.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Bell County property assessment?
sections.html:
Call the Bell County PVA and ask for a conference during the May inspection period. Kentucky requires that conference before you can file an appeal, and it runs for about two weeks beginning the first Monday in May.

If you cannot agree on a value, you file with the Bell County Clerk by the end of the first workday after the inspection period closes. The Department of Revenue gives an example: where the period closes on May 20, the filing deadline is May 21. You must name your own claim of value on the form.

  • Hearings are before a three member local board that sits 25 to 35 days after inspection closes.
  • You supply evidence, such as recent sales of comparable homes, a repair estimate, or an appraisal.
  • The PVA presents the evidence for the assessed value.
  • Notice of the decision comes by certified mail, with instructions for further appeal.

In a county where median value is $89,000, small differences matter. A home in poor condition, with a roof or foundation problem, may be valued like a sound neighbor unless you document the difference.

sections.h2: Who can get the Bell County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or older and owners who are totally disabled can claim the Kentucky homestead exemption on a home they live in. You apply at the Bell County PVA, and approval takes a fixed amount off the assessed value.

The Department of Revenue says the exemption started at $6,500 in 1972 and has been adjusted for inflation every two years since. The Boone County PVA lists the 2026 amount as $49,100, and the Bell County PVA can confirm the figure used on your bill. Applicants must own and maintain the home as their residence, and only one exemption is allowed per household even where both spouses qualify.

  • An approved application stays in force while the original applicant owns and lives in the house.
  • A buyer cannot inherit the seller's exemption; the new owner applies in their own name.
  • Disabled owners under 65 must reapply annually, except service connected disabled veterans and owners permanently disabled under Social Security or state retirement rules.

Where an owner dies, an heir who sells should notify the PVA so the exemption is removed from the address.

sections.h2: What can a Bell County seller do about unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
A seller can pay the bill before closing, or let the title company pay it from the proceeds. Either way the sheriff or the clerk should give a written payoff, because the amount changes by month after April 15.

After that date, the unpaid bill moves to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien. Interest accrues at 1 percent each month, and a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee are added, per the Department of Revenue. Later in the summer the certificate can be sold to a third party at a clerk sale. KRS 134.015 keeps the lien alive for up to 11 years whoever owns the house.

Bell County has three public school districts, Bell County, Middlesboro Independent and Pineville Independent, so ask the sheriff which school district and city rate appear on your parcel's bill. Owners of inherited or vacant houses in Bell County who want to avoid repairs and carrying costs may prefer a cash sale, which settles liens at closing with a written payoff in hand.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Bell County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Bell County Sheriff. City of Pineville tax appears on the same bill as county tax, so one payment covers both.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Bell County assessment?
faqs.a: File with the county clerk no later than one workday after the May inspection period ends. You must first hold a conference with the PVA, and the period starts the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Bell County?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $89,000 for owner occupied homes for 2020 to 2024. Median household income for the same period is $31,354.

faqs.q: What are the late penalties in Bell County?
faqs.a: The normal schedule adds 5 percent in January and a total of 21 percent from February 1 to April 15. After April 15 the clerk adds interest and fees.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Bell County house with a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien stays with the property until it is paid, so the payoff is usually taken from your proceeds at closing. Get the amount in writing from the sheriff or clerk first.
